sources.title: Dialetto genovese (Wikipedia italiana)
sources.reliability_notes: Articles, subject clitics, present of parlâ/dovéi/vende/sentî, ëse/avei/savei/poei, possessives, plurals. The verb table is partly garbled in the extraction; forms used only where cross-checked.

sources.title: Genoese dialect (Wikipedia)
sources.reliability_notes: Orthography (ç, x, æ, eu, circumflex, velar n), articles, pronouns, prepositions (inte, a-o), partitive, voscià/voî, sample sentences.

sources.title: Belin (Wikipedia italiana)
sources.reliability_notes: Meanings and positional uses of belin, derivatives (abelinòu, belinone, me n'imbelino, portâ via o belin), etymology debate (Toso). The article itself notes insufficient citations.

sources.title: belin (Wikizionario)
sources.reliability_notes: Entry marked regional ligure; sense 'male genital organ'; etymology from belo (budello) given as per Devoto-Oli.

sources.title: Proverbi liguri (Wikiquote italiano)
sources.reliability_notes: Proverbs with Italian translations. Spelling is not uniform (mixed Academy and other conventions); used verbatim and normalized only where the rule is documented.

sources.title: Genoese-Italian 'vulgar' phraseology in GEPHRAS and GEPHRAS2
sources.reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed article with register labels [coll.]/[volg.] for Genoese vulgar phrasemes (belin, bagascia, cû, mossa) following Acquarone (2015) spelling; also notes online variants (belìn/belin, cù/cû).
sources.author: Erica Autelli

sources.title: 10 tipici modi di dire e proverbi genovesi
sources.reliability_notes: Local news site; popular selection of sayings, not a linguistic work. Spellings are not Academy.

sources.title: The Most Famous Genoese Words And Phrases
sources.reliability_notes: Popular article; useful for colloquial items (manimàn, cianin cianin, bratta, sciachelo) but spellings are anglicized/italianized.

sources.title: Come parlare ligure
sources.reliability_notes: Travel blog; some items (mugugno, paciugo, quattr'êugg, invexendo, belandi) and two sayings. Low reliability for orthography.

sources.title: Genoese dialect: from belin to bernarda
sources.reliability_notes: Tourist guide piece on 'a few obscene words' (belinon, cuggiun, cuggionà, galuscio); descriptive only.

sources.title: Zena (Wikipedia in ligure)
sources.reliability_notes: Running Genoese prose in the Academy-style orthography (é, ê, -inn-a, -ioìn, ç, x). Used as a model for spelling and article/verb usage.

sources.title: Belin (Wikipedia in ligure)
sources.reliability_notes: Describes belin as the best-known Ligurian word, often a curse but not only; lists abelinòu, belinâta, inbelinâse, pe in bello belìn.

sources.title: Category: Ligurian lemmas / verbs / interjections / nouns (English Wiktionary)
sources.reliability_notes: Attests lemma spellings (andâ, avéi, dovéi, êse, çenâ, giastemâ, poéi, savéi, voéi, alura, bàsta, daghe, merçì, bon giurnu, benvegnûo, belìn, ciùmma...). Inconsistent orthography across entries.

sources.title: Grafia ofiçiâ (zeneize.net, Académia Ligùstica do Brénno)
sources.reliability_notes: Only the introduction was readable: one symbol per sound, 'graphia ofiçiâ' as agreed norm. Subpages (Arfabeto, Acenti) not read; letter values taken from the English Wikipedia articles instead.

sources.title: Ligurian language (Wikipedia)
sources.reliability_notes: Two orthographies (grafia unitäia, grafia ofiçiâ); 25-letter alphabet; vocabulary péi, mei, çetrón, fîgo, éuggio, tésta, bràsso, gànba, cheu.
